# Rabbit Chain

Official website: https://rabbitchain.org
Official GitHub: https://github.com/rabbitmainnet
Official X: https://x.com/rabbit_mainnet

Rabbit Chain is a permissionless EVM Layer 1 powered by LCQ Consensus. Rabbit Testnet (Chain ID 9280) is the first public network. Rabbit Mainnet (Chain ID 928) follows validation.
Rabbit Core Testnet v2.4.16 upgrade: v2.4.16 (source commit d9815e734239a021e0faa51d5e58c58457888db5).
Rabbit Core v2.4.16 retains verified automatic multipart blockchain bootstrap, resumable downloads, progress reporting and wallet-first initialization for new miners. Existing miners retain their data. Earlier releases added authenticated encrypted DKG evaluations and verified VRF partial signatures through public peers when miners have no direct connection. This release schedules WorkSeat liveness V2 at block 323,800. The VRF economics and WorkSeat admission activation remains block 320,000. Availability V2 activated at block 173057 in v2.4.6. Any user or contract can request VRF without mining. Earlier fork heights and the existing genesis, wallets and blockchain data are preserved. Keep the operating-system clock synchronized. VRF completion must be verified through canonical request status, randomness and proof; local key creation alone is not completion.
Rabbit VRF DKG preparation started at block 136065. Rabbit VRF protocol and the VRF liveness rules activated at block 136193. Protocol activation is distinct from verified fulfillment. Public request testing is experimental: inspect canonical completion before using randomness.

Extracting software on another drive does not move the data directory. Rabbit Core supports --data-dir; existing users must stop all Rabbit processes, copy the complete data directory and verify their existing wallet before using another location.

Key routes: /testnet, /mainnet, /lcq, /platform, /developers, /docs, /security, /releases, /status.

Earlier releases preserved the Availability V2 schedule on restart; v2.4.16 preserves the historical block 320000 schedule and adds WorkSeat liveness V2 at block 323800.

Earlier releases improved live block import and production recovery: nodes briefly wait for an incoming direct-extension block before starting recovery, and a shorter conflicting peer no longer keeps production paused. Historical fork heights and mining rewards remain unchanged; VRF economics and WorkSeat admission remain active from block 320,000.

Earlier releases isolated outgoing LCQ messages in bounded per-peer queues so a slow peer does not block delivery to other peers. It retries failed asynchronous recovery downloads and reports canonical penalties in English, including the end block and remaining blocks. Normal operational status refreshes approximately every 10 to 12 seconds.
PENALIZED reports missed assigned production turns, the canonical penalty end block and remaining blocks. It does not prove the underlying technical cause. Penalty expiry still requires synchronization and selection.

Rabbit Core v2.4.16 schedules WorkSeat liveness V2 at public Testnet block 323800. VRF economics V2 and WorkSeat admission V2 remain active from block 320000. Keep existing chain data, wallets and identities. New installations retain the verified multipart bootstrap. Block target remains 10 seconds; mining rewards remain 70/30.
From block 320000 the VRF base pricing target is US$0.005 equivalent in tRUSD, payable in tRAB using quoteRequestFee(0), plus gas. At fulfillment, 50% plus rounding goes to development allocation, 30% to validated VRF signers and 20% to the fulfillment block producer.
Two local SSD-backed tests completed 48 valid requests with three concurrent clients; early-proof verification took 0.176–1.242 seconds after observed inclusion. These local results do not establish public-network throughput, a latency SLA or consensus finality. The existing web timer tracks on-chain fulfillment.

WorkSeat liveness V2: upgrade to Rabbit Core v2.4.16 before block 323800. The correction allows an authorized fallback to account for missed turns when an admitted WorkSeat lacks registry bookkeeping. Existing VRF rules, genesis, wallets and mining reward split are preserved. Local tests observed 10 to 13 second intervals; this is not a public-network timing guarantee.
